definitions.explanation: A train service faster than a regular express. Originally referred to the first Shinkansen services.

definitions.gloss: at top speed; in a huge rush; extremely fast
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively to describe doing something at maximum speed or completing a task in an extremely short time.

examples.japanese: {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{東京|とうきょう}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: I headed to Tokyo on the super express.

examples.japanese: {新幹線|しんかんせん}は{超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}として{開業|かいぎょう}した。
examples.english: The Shinkansen was launched as a super express service.

examples.japanese: この{電車|でんしゃ}は{超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}だから{途中|とちゅう}{停車|ていしゃ}が{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: This train is a super express, so it makes few intermediate stops.

examples.japanese: {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{仕上|しあ}げてください。
examples.english: Please finish it at top speed.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りが{近|ちか}いので{超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{作業|さぎょう}した。
examples.english: The deadline was close, so I worked at top speed.

examples.japanese: {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{企画書|きかくしょ}をまとめたので、{内容|ないよう}に{不安|ふあん}が{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: I put together the proposal at breakneck speed, so I'm still uneasy about the content.

notes:
Composed of {超|ちょう} (super, ultra) + {特急|とっきゅう} (limited express). Originally a railway term for trains faster than {特急|とっきゅう}, notably the first Shinkansen in 1964. Now commonly used figuratively to mean doing something extremely fast.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{仕上|しあ}げる: to finish at top speed
- {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{対応|たいおう}する: to respond at maximum speed
- {超特急|ちょうとっきゅう}で{届|とど}ける: to deliver at top speed

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {特急|とっきゅう}: limited express — the standard fast train service; also used figuratively but with less intensity
- {急行|きゅうこう}: express — slower than {特急|とっきゅう}
- {大至急|だいしきゅう}: extremely urgent — similar figurative meaning but focused on urgency rather than speed
